Looking at panel c, the outer ring of each donut chart represents the "old" population. In the old microglia chart, the yellow segment (Phospholipids) dominates the ring, occupying well over half of the proportions. In the old liver chart, Phospholipids makes up a much smaller fraction, with Glycerolipids and Cholesterol esters being comparatively larger. Thus Phospholipids show the largest proportional difference between old microglia and old liver.

[ANSWER]G[/ANSWER]

Let me look at panel c. There are two donut charts: microglia and liver. Each has two rings - outer ring "old" and inner ring "young" (based on the labels "old" pointing to outer and "young" pointing to inner).

The legend: Glycerolipids (green), Phospholipids (yellow/orange), Ceramide (blue), Sphingomyeline (red), Cholesterol esters (brown), FFA (purple).

Now I need to compare old microglia (outer ring of microglia) vs old liver (outer ring of liver).

Looking at microglia outer ring (old): It's dominated by yellow (Phospholipids) - very large portion, then green (Glycerolipids), then brown (Cholesterol esters), blue (Ceramide), red (Sphingomyeline), purple (FFA).

Looking at liver outer ring (old): It has green (Glycerolipids) substantial, brown (Cholesterol esters) substantial, yellow (Phospholipids) moderate, red (Sphingomyeline) notable, blue small.

So in old microglia, Phospholipids (yellow) is the dominant class, taking up maybe >50% of the ring. In old liver, Phospholipids is much smaller (maybe ~25-30%), with Glycerolipids and Cholesterol esters being larger.

Thus the lipid type more prevalent in old microglia compared to old liver with greatest difference is Phospholipids.

Let me double check by examining the visual proportions. In microglia outer ring, yellow is huge (left half plus more). In liver outer ring, yellow is a smaller chunk. So the difference in proportion for Phospholipids is largest.

Thus answer G.

Let me confirm options: G = Phospholipids. Yes.

Therefore answer [ANSWER]G[/ANSWER].
